concepts.title: Endpoint masses and frame locations
concepts.description: The first link ends at the elbow, while the second ends at the tool tip. Their masses are idealized at those two points.

concepts.title: Zero COM inertia does not mean zero joint inertia
concepts.description: A zero COM inertia tensor removes the local spin moment I alpha + omega×I omega, not the moment r×ma about a displaced joint.
concepts.subtopic: Zero COM inertia does not mean zero joint inertia

concepts.title: Terminal boundary and gravity initialization
concepts.description: A fixed base, gravity compensation and moving joints coexist. Zero terminal wrench removes only the boundary contact load.

concepts.title: Direction of successive frame rotations
concepts.description: Changing from frame1 to frame2 uses the transpose of the frame2-to-frame1 rotation.

concepts.title: First-link angular propagation
concepts.description: With omega0=0, only q1dot z1 remains in the outward recursion.

concepts.title: Angular acceleration transport
concepts.description: The vanishing term is a parallel-axis kinematic fact. It does not imply zero accelerations or zero centripetal forces.

concepts.title: Gravity-augmented origin acceleration
concepts.description: The vector here includes fictitious gravity compensation. It is not the physical acceleration of the fixed base origin.

concepts.title: Tangential and centripetal acceleration
concepts.description: For a +z axis, z×x=y and z×y=−x. The nested product therefore points radially inward.

concepts.title: First-link COM acceleration and force
concepts.description: The first mass needs both inward centripetal force and tangential-plus-gravity support force.

concepts.title: COM spin moment versus transmitted joint moment
concepts.description: The zero COM tensors remove local rotational inertia moments, while offset forces generate moments about joints.
concepts.subtopic: COM spin moment versus transmitted joint moment

concepts.title: Inherited and relative angular motion
concepts.description: Both parallel revolute joints contribute to the second link’s absolute angular motion.

concepts.title: When the first COM equals the elbow origin
concepts.description: Point-mass idealization alone is insufficient. The specified distal location makes the first COM coincide with the next frame origin.
concepts.subtopic: When the first COM equals the elbow origin

concepts.title: Gravity projection and angle-sum shorthand
concepts.description: The expanded gravity terms are g cos(theta2) sin(theta1)+g sin(theta2) cos(theta1), equal to g sin(theta1+theta2).

concepts.title: Frame2 origin acceleration
concepts.description: The elbow acceleration contains first-link tangential/centripetal effects plus gravity, expressed in the second frame.

concepts.title: Second COM acceleration from the elbow
concepts.description: Both the moving elbow and the second link’s absolute angular motion contribute to its distal mass acceleration.
concepts.subtopic: Second COM acceleration from the elbow

concepts.title: Squaring the absolute angular rate
concepts.description: The second link rotates at the sum of the two joint rates; squaring that sum produces the mixed velocity contribution.

concepts.title: Zero link2 spin does not mean zero COM acceleration
concepts.description: Equal and opposite joint rates can cancel the second link’s absolute rotation while leaving translational motion inherited from the elbow.
concepts.subtopic: Zero link2 spin does not mean zero COM acceleration

concepts.title: Second-link force and COM spin moment
concepts.description: Newton’s force equation retains the finite point mass, while Euler’s local spin moment is zero at that point.
concepts.subtopic: Second-link force and COM spin moment

concepts.title: Why terminal link force equals its mass force
concepts.description: The terminal boundary removes the rotated downstream-force term only for this particular example.
concepts.subtopic: Why terminal link force equals its mass force

concepts.title: Distal joint moment from the mass force
concepts.description: Only the transverse force component contributes about the elbow z axis.
concepts.subtopic: Distal joint moment from the mass force

concepts.title: Rotate the downstream force before adding
concepts.description: The inward pass rotates from frame2 back into frame1 before adding the own-link force.
concepts.subtopic: Rotate the downstream force before adding

concepts.title: Separate own and downstream moment arms
concepts.description: The elbow transmits both a force and a moment. The first mass adds its own force moment about the base joint.
concepts.subtopic: Separate own and downstream moment arms

concepts.title: Checking the printed vector transpose
concepts.description: The dimensionally consistent general recursion and the following expansion both use a column moment vector. The visible extra transpose is preserved as a source caveat, not silently adopted.

concepts.title: Expanding the moment-arm rotation product
concepts.description: The row extracts the correct frame1 y component of the rotated downstream force and multiplies by l1.

concepts.title: Gravity combination in the first-joint moment
concepts.description: The downstream gravity force’s first-link lever arm depends on theta1 after both coordinate projections are combined.
concepts.subtopic: Gravity combination in the first-joint moment

concepts.title: Cancellation of the first squared-rate torque term
concepts.description: The absence of a pure q1dot² term in tau1 is a cancellation between transmitted and offset-force moments, not a gravity or zero-inertia simplification.
concepts.subtopic: Cancellation of the first squared-rate torque term

concepts.title: Extracting the signed actuator torque
concepts.description: Joint torque is the signed moment component along the permitted rotation axis, not a generic moment magnitude.

concepts.title: Computing both actuator torques
concepts.description: Compute inertia, velocity-product and gravity contributions separately before adding them; this avoids losing the asymmetric velocity terms.

concepts.title: Collecting the joint-space inertia matrix
concepts.description: Both acceleration cross-couplings come from the second mass and have identical coefficients.

concepts.title: Kinematic singularity versus inertia singularity
concepts.description: Loss of an instantaneous Cartesian direction does not erase the independent kinetic energy of two positive endpoint masses.

concepts.title: Static gravity compensation
concepts.description: The required actuator torques oppose physical gravity and are positive under the chosen counterclockwise angle convention.

concepts.title: Simultaneous reversal of joint rates
concepts.description: The model has velocity-product inertial terms but no friction term odd in velocity. Simultaneous rate reversal leaves all displayed torque terms unchanged.

concepts.title: Nonzero coupling torque at a joint with zero acceleration

concepts.title: Inputs to inverse dynamics
concepts.description: The calculation evaluates actuator requirements for a prescribed motion and boundary load. It does not integrate an unknown future trajectory.

concepts.title: Outward then inward Newton–Euler passes
concepts.description: Motion propagates outward from the base; required loads propagate inward from the prescribed terminal boundary.

sourceIssues.description: The phrase “No external force acting” is immediately followed by gravity inclusion. Interpret it as no externally applied terminal wrench, not absence of gravitational body forces. The +g Y0 base seed is a gravity bookkeeping device, not actual base acceleration.
The text attributes p12=pC1 to a point mass. More precisely this equality needs the stated distal-end location; a point mass placed elsewhere on link1 would not make its COM coincide with the elbow.

A transpose superscript is printed after a vertically arranged 3x1 n2 vector in an expanded R12 n2 product. Applying it literally makes a3x3 times1x3 product invalid. Use the dimensionally consistent general recursion and the next page’s column-vector expansion, and disclose the printing inconsistency.
